findings.fact: Both ordinary and terminal production reconciliation call canonicalizePhysicalObjects with the persistent registry.

For multi-node identity groups mergeObjectAttributes executes BEFORE registry.applyPhysicalGeometry; the legacy support1000/max/motion gate is therefore computationally reachable, not a wholly dead compatibility branch.

If a current fragment exists, registry write-back overwrites mesh, bounding box, position, reconstruction support and motion details. The prior temporary legacy holder does not own the displayed current geometry.

If there are closed fragments but no current fragment, write-back empties mesh and resets support, but does not replace bounding box/position. Those fields can retain the legacy-selected holder. It is not sound to declare the entire support gate unobservable.
Presence right boundary/trajectory derive from newest direct observations, separately from geometry support. Do not replace this interval construction while editing support selection.

mathematical_boundary: Frame count and missing-detail sentinel1000 are source-selection heuristics, not a calibrated probability of geometry correctness. Dynamic-history bit is also not a calibrated emission (P16). Registry q must not be substituted for source-confidence.
next: Inspect consumers of closed-state bbox/position and null-registry callers before a single source-selection trial; use shared source provenance and actual confidence only if identifiable. Preserve registry authority and intervals.
counting: Reachability preflight, not a completed probabilistic rewrite or a failed code trial.
